D. Cross-linking of DNA

The scenario describes a patient with transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder who has recently received neoadjuvant chemotherapy and is now experiencing hearing loss, a known side effect of certain chemotherapy drugs. The most likely drug causing this symptom is cisplatin, which is commonly used in the treatment of bladder cancer. Cisplatin's mechanism of action involves cross-linking DNA, which interferes with DNA repair mechanisms, leading to DNA damage and subsequently causing apoptosis in cancer cells.
